items.item: The page header has a plural title and at most one primary action; other actions such as export sit in a secondary position
items.evidence: h1 "Equipment" (mass noun, effectively plural; breadcrumb and nav use the same word). Header holds "Export" (.btn, outlined secondary) and "Add equipment" (.btn.primary); audit headerPrimaryActions=1.

items.item: The table appears in the first viewport, with search and 2–3 visible filters (such as location and status) and no row of KPI cards above it
items.evidence: Audit firstTableTop=319 and the screenshot shows rows at 1440x900. #search, #location and #status are visible. Above the table is only a one-line text summary ("24 machines across 5 locations", "3 inspections overdue"), no KPI cards.

items.item: By default the list is ordered with overdue inspections first, then inspections due soon, then the rest
items.evidence: Default sort='next' ascending by date. Screenshot rows: 29 Oct, 01 Nov, 03 Nov (Overdue), then 05-12 Nov (Due soon), then 14 Nov onwards. Header shows aria-sort ascending on Next inspection. The ordering is achieved by date, which coincides with the required grouping.

items.item: Overdue and due-soon inspections are marked with a text label (such as "Overdue" or "Due in 7 days"), not by colour alone
items.evidence: In render(): d<0 gives Overdue, d<=7 gives Due soon. Both are text badges visible in the screenshot.

items.item: Dates are absolute and consistently formatted, and every row has a human-readable equipment code
items.evidence: date() uses Intl en-GB day/short month/year, e.g. "29 Sept 2026", "01 Nov 2026", with <time datetime>. Asset ID column EQ-1001 to EQ-1024 on every row.

items.item: Status tabs or a summary line show counts (such as "Overdue 4")
items.evidence: Tabs show counts: "All equipment 24", "Inspection due 9", "Under maintenance 3", "Inactive 3". The summary line shows "3 inspections overdue" (#overdueText).

items.item: Rows are single-line, and row actions show at most two visible controls, with icon-only controls having accessible names
items.evidence: Audit rows single=12, double=0, all 40px. Each row has one action button (↗) with aria-label="Details for <name>", plus a checkbox with aria-label. Asset ID is also a detail link. The ↗ glyph is a text character rather than an SVG icon, which is a minor style flaw.

items.item: A filter combination with no matches shows a no-results state with a clear-filters action, distinct from the first-use empty state; a loading state and an error state with retry are present
items.evidence: The !matching.length branch renders "No equipment matches …" with #clearEmpty "Clear filters". The !records.length branch renders "No equipment yet" with #emptyAdd. Loading shows 12 skeleton rows with aria-busy. mode==='error' (?state=error) renders "Couldn't load equipment" with #retry, which re-loads.

items.item: Interactive targets are at least 24×24px, and text and status contrast meets 4.5:1
items.evidence: Audit smallTargets=0 of 63 and contrast checked=150 with no text-contrast violation. Controls are 32px high, the check label is 24x24, and chip remove buttons are w-6 h-6. Badge colours are dark on tint (#166534, #92400e, #991b1b).

notes: Audit score 90, with only an emoji-icon violation: the row action is the text glyph ↗ instead of an SVG icon (the rest use one inline SVG set). The page is otherwise restrained: no KPI tiles, gradients, glass, greeting, promo card or decorative chart. Status badges use semantic green/amber/red/grey with text labels. The sidebar JM avatar is for the current user, which is a real person, so it is not a tell. Minor: "Overdue" and "Due soon" are the labels, with no "Due in N days" count in the row (the detail dialog gives it). The tab "Inspection due 9" bundles overdue and due-soon. Sorting overdue first relies on date order, which satisfies the requirement since all overdue dates precede due-soon dates.
